citations.claim: At step 16 the pole angle is 0.826 rad (margin -0.026), violating the 0.8 rad pole_upright limit.
System energy grew to ~7.78 by step 16 from ~1.32 initial with no pushes, showing destabilization.
One step before failure the pole was already at 0.718 rad with high angular rate, showing rapid divergence.

counterfactual.change: Set sensor_noise from 0.01789 to 0.0 only; same 16 steps. Failure disappears, so noisy angle feedback caused the destabilization.

explanation: With high sensor_noise (~0.018) and large dt (~0.0187), the state-feedback controller receives corrupted pole-angle measurements each outer step and applies incorrect forces (e.g. +2.73 at step 16). With no pushes, energy grows from ~1.32 to ~7.78 and pole rate reaches ~5.8 rad/s by step 16, swinging the pole from -0.07 to +0.826 rad beyond the 0.8 limit. Removing only the noise prevents the failure, confirming noise-induced loss of balance.
vision_note: The cart stays near the center of the track while the pole leans progressively farther to the right from steps 13 to 15. At step 16 the pole tip turns red, showing the pole has tipped beyond the upright limit.
